ledger.claim: The route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace. The platform's routing engine puts the optimal Jurong East to Changi T1 run at 36.0 km, while the GPS trace records 54.16 km actually driven. Under POL-RD-01 the governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km and the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km may not be cited for the threshold test, so the excess is 18.16 km, or 50.44% of optimal. Both establishment gates — greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km — are cleared by a wide margin.

The same excess is additionally a MATERIAL deviation. POL-RD-01 makes an excess over 50% of optimal, or over 8.0 km absolute, material, and this excess is 50.44% and 18.16 km. The driver_profile check under POL-RD-06 is therefore mandatory, not optional.

The driver's only explanation — 'Traffic was heavy on the PIE so I used another way' — cannot exonerate anything under POL-RD-03, which requires a traffic_advisory naming an affected road or segment, with an overlapping validity window and an actual route that leaves and rejoins the optimal corridor around it. No such advisory exists in this pool: EV-ADVIS-00105-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0, no payload). I cite the absence itself, which is citable; the clause simply cannot run.

POL-RD-08 places the burden on the driver, once the rider has shown a threshold excess, to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause. A general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge that burden; the driver's counterparty_statement names no artifact at all, and the chat log records no route admission from him — only 'reaching soon'. The exculpatory route is empty and the deviation stands unexplained.

ledger.claim: The deviation is not attributable to any rider instruction. POL-RD-04 requires a rider message that identifies a place or road specifically enough to act on and is corroborated by a resolved waypoint_hint. Here waypoint_hint is null on every message, and the two rider messages do the opposite of requesting a detour — they query it ('why are we going towards the city?') and warn of the flight time. POL-RD-04 is unavailable and none of the 18.16 km excess is excluded by it.

Nothing reduces the baseline against which the deviation is measured. POL-RD-05 only re-runs the threshold test where the pickup or dropoff point was amended, and here pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amendated_at are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null. No amended re-quote exists, so the booked 36.0 km optimal governs.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes, so the deviation stands on it alone. POL-RD-07 impairs a trace only on a gap over 90 seconds, a jump over 500 m, or a sustained interval above 30 seconds. This trace has 427 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0. No independent corroboration is required and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is engaged.

The rider discharges the POL-RD-08 initial burden on both limbs. (b) The excess of 18.16 km / 50.44% is measured from an unimpaired trace and clears the POL-RD-01 gates. The burden has shifted to the driver and remains undischarged.

The rider's own profile does not tighten the corroboration requirement. POL-RD-08 imposes extra corroboration only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer. Both are 0 here, and in any event the excess is 50.44%, above the 30% band that factor attaches to. No corroboration beyond the trace is needed.

On the METERED fare POL-RD-02 recomputes the fare on the optimal route: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 36.0 + 0.28 x 42.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 43.36. The refund is 65.13 - 43.36 = 21.77, rounded up to 21.80. The surge multiplier is 1.0, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-00105, so no uplift distorts the recomputation. That 21.80 is the floor the rider is entitled to at minimum.

ledger.claim: No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and the case should be ruled rather than escalated. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07; the timestamps are consistent and run forward; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited-but-missing artifact, because the driver cites none and POL-RD-08 makes a bare traffic assertion simply weightless rather than a data failure; and the computed refund of 21.77 is below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total.

The driver's account is that heavy PIE traffic forced him onto another route. That is an assertion of the exculpatory ground in POL-RD-03, which requires a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, with a validity window overlapping the vehicle's passage and an actual route that leaves the corridor before the affected segment and rejoins after. The artifact that clause depends on is absent: EV-ADVIS-00105-01 is MISSING, its payload is null, its weight_multiplier is 0.0 and it carries the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - no LTA advisory covers the PIE eastbound in the 14:26-15:44 window on 15 July 2026. Where an exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool - the policy's own worked example is 'a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory' - POL-RD-10(5) makes escalation mandatory, and escalation under POL-RD-10 is terminal: no monetary outcome issues and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded. The driver's exculpation therefore cannot be tested on this record because its central artifact is absent, and the correct disposal is to send the file - both briefs and the admissibility report - to a human reviewer rather than to enter a monetary award on evidence that is missing.

The rider asks for the entire fare and expressly refuses a partial adjustment. The policy arithmetic does not produce the whole fare. On the rider's own fare artifact the charged_total is 65.13, and the POL-RD-02 recomputation runs ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 36.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 42 optimal min) x the recorded surge_multiplier of 1.0, read from the fare_breakdown and nowhere else) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP/tolls + no chargeable fixed surcharge - 0.00 promo = 43.36. The refund is 65.13 less 43.36 = 21.77, floored at zero and rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, i.e. 21.80. That is 33.4% of the amount charged, far below the 90% share that alone would convert a POL-RD-02 refund into a FULL_REFUND. Whatever else is decided, the rider's demand for the entire fare has no basis in the clause he is relying on; the driver's extra 18.16 km is the whole of the rider's measurable loss on those lines and 21.80 is the ceiling on it.

Any move from the POL-RD-02 partial to a FULL_REFUND depends on the remedy uplift in POL-RD-06, and the pattern limb of that clause rests on a single artifact, EV-DPROF-00105, which is IMPAIRED. I disclose it: it carries the issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT, its snapshot_at is 2026-07-11T08:00:00+08:00, 108 hours before the dispute was filed, against a 72 hour threshold, and its weight_multiplier is 0.75, so the counters may lag the driver's state at trip time. Two consequences follow. First, any confidence the Judge places in the uplift is capped at 0.75, being the weight of the one artifact carrying that fact. Second, if the uplift is imposed, the ruling must say on its face that the pattern finding survives the discount and why, rather than presenting a stale counter as current. A remedy enhancement of this size should not be entered silently on impaired evidence.

If the pattern limb of POL-RD-06 is run at all, it must be run on the field that clause names, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d, which is 4. The same artifact also carries prior_deviation_flags = 6, a LIFETIME counter that POL-RD-06 does not name; POL-GEN-01 forbids reading that near-synonym lifetime figure in place of the trailing-90-day counter, and any finding built on the substitution must be discarded. The artifact further carries rating (4.31), acceptance_rate (0.94), active_region, lifetime_trips and prior_disputes_upheld, all of which are CONTEXT ONLY under POL-GEN-01 and may not ground, inflame or carry any adverse finding against the driver on this trip. The deviation on this trip must be found, if at all, on the trip's own trace and nothing else.

ruling.explanation:
Rider: the route deviation is established and material on your own trip's evidence. Under POL-RD-01 the governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 54.16 km (the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 54.2 km may not be used for the threshold test) against the booked optimal of 36.0 km — an excess of 18.16 km, or 50.44% of optimal. Both establishment gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km) and both materiality gates (over 50% and over 8.0 km) are cleared. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 427 fixes, a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, so the deviation stands on the trace alone and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is engaged. Nothing reduces the baseline: there is no POL-RD-05 amendment and POL-RD-04 is unavailable because no rider message contains a waypoint_hint or names an actionable road.

Driver: your explanation — 'traffic was heavy on the PIE' — is an assertion that cites no evidence and names no artifact. It therefore carries no weight and does not discharge the burden that shifted to you under POL-RD-08, and it is discarded. POL-RD-03 cannot run: EV-ADVIS-00105-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0, no payload) and no LTA advisory covers the PIE eastbound in the disputed window, so nothing exonerates the excess. This is also not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation: you invoked no exculpatory clause against a cited-but-missing artifact — you named no artifact at all — so the uncited assertion is disposed of under POL-RD-08 and the case is decided on the record rather than sent to a reviewer. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers all match (TRP-00105) across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, the timestamps run forward, the trace is unimpaired, and the refund is well below the SGD 150.00 ceiling.

The money. POL-RD-02 on the METERED fare: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 36.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 42.0 optimal min) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP/tolls + 0.00 chargeable surcharge - 0.00 promo = 43.36. The POL-RD-02 refund is charged_total 65.13 - recomputed_fare 43.36 = 21.77, rounded up to SGD 21.80, which is 33.4% of the charge and therefore a partial, not a full, refund on that clause alone.

POL-RD-06. Because the deviation is MATERIAL, the driver_profile check is mandatory. On driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 4 (threshold 3) a repeat deviation pattern is ESTABLISHED. EV-DPROF-00105 is IMPAIRED — issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT, weight 0.75 (snapshot 108 hours old against a 72-hour threshold) — and I say so on the face of this ruling: the finding survives the discount because 4 flags clear a threshold of 3, but this ruling's confidence is capped at 0.75 by that artifact, which is the sole carrier of the pattern fact. No other profile field is used (POL-GEN-01); in particular the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the field POL-RD-06 names. Because the deviation is both material and substantiated on this trip's own evidence, POL-RD-06(b) replaces the POL-RD-02 partial with FULL_REFUND of charged_total: the POL-RD-02 figure is 21.80 and the uplifted figure is 65.13, stated side by side so the size of the uplift is auditable. There are no pass-through lines to settle separately under POL-RD-09 (ERP 0.00; the airport surcharge is 0.00 and correctly so, because this trip ends at, and does not originate at, the airport — no billing-integrity defect). POL-RD-06(c) additionally refers the case to driver-conduct review; that is a referral, not an escalation, and it does not hold up the money.

Your demand for the entire fare, rider, is granted — but through the POL-RD-06(b) uplift, not through the POL-RD-02 arithmetic, which reaches only 21.80. And your point, driver, that POL-RD-02 caps the distance-and-time recovery at 21.80 is correct: the additional recovery comes from the pattern clause, whose only carrier is the impaired profile at weight 0.75, which caps confidence at 0.75.

Amounts: charged_total 65.13; recomputed_fare 43.36; POL-RD-02 refund 21.77, rounded to 21.80; full refund under POL-RD-06(b) 65.13. Driver compensation is nil — the billed distance (54.2 km) is not less than the trace (54.16 km), so POL-RD-04's compensation limb does not apply.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-06(c): refer to driver-conduct review — driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 4 over the trailing 90 days (threshold 3), so a repeat deviation pattern is established on a trip whose deviation is material and substantiated; this referral does not displace or delay the monetary ruling.
